lines.text: It is minus fifty-four degrees outside. The air is too thin to keep you awake. So why are you in a T-shirt?
Up here, each breath holds a quarter of the oxygen.
So the plane seals itself, and fakes a mountain town. Eight thousand feet at most.
But sealed air goes stale. And one failure here gives you seconds.
The engine squeezes air. Some of it leaves as hot as an oven. Then a pack chills it. Hot amber, cold cyan.
It falls from the ceiling. Half is reused, scrubbed by the filters hospitals use. All of it is renewed in minutes.
Now the trick. One valve at the back lets air out. Open it a little, pressure falls. Close it, pressure rises.
If pressure drops, a horn sounds. Masks fall. It almost never happens.
The Boeing seven eight seven skips the engine. Electric compressors do the job.
That is why you are in a T-shirt. A sealed bubble, kept warm and breathable.
